properties.name: Something notices an idea that connects to nothing
properties.rationale:
Anthony chose option (b) of `dec:idea-what-notices-an-idea-that-connects-to-nothing` on 2026-08-21, and asked for the idea to be brainstormed, linked, accepted and then built — which is what happened, in that order.

THE PREREQUISITE WAS PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE, not a caveat on it. The skill asked for "no real relation" in PROSE, and prose cannot be told apart from silence. So the first thing built was a structural home for the judgement: `Decision.no_relation_note`. Everything else rests on it.

⭐ WHAT THE BRAINSTORM ITSELF PROVED, and it is the reason the linking step exists. Four searches run before writing turned up a COLLISION nobody had noticed — brainstorm/SKILL.md step 2 forbids running detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes, and a detector on unlinked ideas is exactly that — and then turned up its RESOLUTION, `req:detecting-is-not-asking`, written eleven days earlier. Neither node mentioned the other. BOTH halves of that finding came out of the near-matches the linking step spends, not out of thinking harder.

MEASURED AFTER LINKING: against a population where 115 of 147 ideas reach zero other ideas within two hops, the newly captured idea reached 2 at one hop, 4 at two and 9 at three. That is the "one search instead of four" Anthony described, working.

THE THREE STATES THE BUILD DISTINGUISHES: linked; reviewed and deliberately unlinked; nobody looked. Only the third is a finding. Fourteen tests exist mostly to pin that boundary — a blank note is not an answer, one bad link writes none of them, and a detector with nothing to run on says nothing rather than reporting "0 of 0".

NOT BUILT, AND DELIBERATELY: cluster search, the second half Anthony named. It was measured to be ORDERED AFTER this one — built before linking existed it would have returned nothing for 77% of ideas, which reads as a broken feature rather than an unlinked graph.
properties.summary: review_relations records what a node relates to or that nothing does, and unreviewed_ideas reports the proposed decisions carrying neither.
